content: The prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) among individuals with type 2 diabetes is approximately 23%, with up to 58% experiencing some form of sleep-disordered breathing. In individuals with obesity who participated in the Look AHEAD trial, the prevalence of OSA was even higher, exceeding 80%. Patients exhibiting symptoms of OSA, such as excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, or observed episodes of apnea during sleep, should undergo appropriate screening for the condition. Treatment options for sleep apnea include lifestyle modifications, the use of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) devices, oral appliances, and surgical interventions. These treatments have been demonstrated to improve quality of life and aid in the management of blood pressure. However, the evidence regarding a direct impact of OSA treatment on glycemic control remains inconclusive.
